text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Protesters go on the streets of Belgrade and other Serbian towns for 21th day running over annulled election results while the Serbian Supreme Court rejects appeals to overturn the annullment.
- A demonstrator who was carrying the effigy of President Slobodan Milosevic was imprisoned and badly beaten.

- Prospects for Yugoslavia's access to the International Monetary Fund are good but it is still being put in a political context, says head of Yugoslav government team for talks with the Fund Oskar Kovac.

- The dinar drops considerably on the black market exchange rate over the weekend. The mark was exchanged for almost four dinars against the 3.5 dinars so far. Still no explanation for the jump or whether it is going to last.
- Montenegrin ships will stay blocked in U.S. ports while outer wall of sanctions remain in place.
- Niksic steel plant celebrates 40th anniversary. The plant's annual capacity is 320,000 tonnes of crude steel and 280,000 tonnes of final products.

- After four rounds of local elections the left coalition-- Socialist Party of Serbia, Jugoslav left and New Democracy-- wins 66 out of 110 seats in the Belgrade assembly, says municipal electoral commission.

- Smederevo steel complex Sartid 1913 production this year will be 500,000 tonnes of finished products, which is five times more than the previous year, says production manager Branko Grujic. Some 70 percent of the production is for exports.
- Yugoslav trade minister Djordje Siradovic left Sunday for a three-day visit to China.
- The new Yugoslav parliament to hold its constituent session on Tuesday.
